title.narrative: Punjab Intermediate Cities Improvement Investment Project

description.narrative: The project will improve the quality of life of the residents in the intermediate cities of Sahiwal and Sialkot in Punjab Province, making these cities more livable and sustainable. This will be achieved by improving urban infrastructure and services, and operations and maintenance capacity for urban service delivery.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Access to quality urban services by the residents of Sahiwal and Sialkot cities improved

Volume of wastewater treatment increased to at least 80,000 cubic meters per day in Sahiwal and Sialkot (2016 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Sanitation sector master plan were prepared and approved for both cities. Priority schemes were identified. $44.8 million and $32.1 million contracts were awarded for improvement of sanitation system in Sahiwal and Sialkot city respectively. Works have reached final phase of completion and handover of the assets to the respective utilities' companies have commenced.
$10.11million WWTP contract for Sialkot was awarded in Q4-2021 and letter of commencement issued after substantial implementation of LARPs, validation of external safeguards expert and approval of ADB CWRD's Safeguards unit. Works on Sialkot WWTP are ongoing and expected to be completed in Q2-2026.
WWTP Sahiwal package was terminated in Q2 2023, as the contractor failed to proceed with the works without reasonable excuse. This package was re-bid and re-awarded in Q2 2024 for $8.67 million. Letter of commencement issued after substantial implementation of LARPs, validation of external safeguards expert and approval of ADB CWRD's Safeguards unit. Works on Sahiwal WWTP are ongoing and expected to be completed in Q2-2026. Data Source: ADB Project Completion Report Actual value:

Works have reached final phase of completion and handover of the assets to the respective utilities' companies have commenced. Data Source: ADB Project Completion Report Actual value:

Priority schemes were identified. WATSAN subprojects in both cities (08 Contracts) were awarded. All outputs listed here are covered through two (02) of these eight (08) contracts. Works for the water supply component under these two (02) contracts commenced in early 2021 and are near completion and asset handover started. Data Source: Annual report of the project Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y

Based on Consultant's determination (endorsed by EA) post paid instead of prepaid water meters are planned to be procured by the Government.
